begin-concept: A person standing in a cluttered study, gently untangling a large knotted ball of thread that becomes neat parallel lines as it leaves their hands; a window with soft daylight.
begin-example: A person at a kitchen table glancing at a wall clock and a calendar while putting on a coat, a small tangled ribbon-shaped thought cloud gently unravelling into a simple ribbon.
picture-concept: A tabletop model of a street junction made of buttons and matchsticks, with a faint ghostly image of real cars at the same junction hovering above it, dotted lines linking each button to a car.
picture-example: Two friends at a café table, one pushing a salt shaker and a pepper shaker across the tablecloth to re-enact a small car accident, the other leaning in to watch.
facts-concept: Two side-by-side panels of the same desk with the same three objects (a cup, a book, a lamp); in one the cup rests on the book, in the other it sits on a shelf.
facts-example: A hand lifting a coffee cup off a closed book on a tidy desk and placing it on a shelf, motion suggested with soft curved lines.
logic-concept: A calm landscape split down the middle: rain on one side, sunshine on the other, with a single umbrella-shaped sign in the centre covering both halves equally.
logic-example: A person looking at a phone whose screen shows half a raincloud and half a sun, shrugging with a gentle, amused expression.
limits-concept: A wooden ladder leaning against a high stone wall in a meadow, a figure at the top looking out over a wide view, the ladder about to be set aside.
limits-example: Two friends laughing together at a café table while a third person looks at a notebook of written-out explanations, puzzled.
ethics-concept: A large old book open on a lectern, its pages filled with precise measurements and charts, while a small figure outside the window helps someone carry groceries; warm light falls on the helper, not the book.
ethics-example: A kitchen knife slicing a tomato cleanly on one side of the image; on the other, a person holding a door open for an elderly neighbour.
builders-concept: Two builders on a sunny building site: one calls out with a raised hand while the other carries a large stone slab toward them; stacks of blocks, pillars and beams around.
builders-example: An operating theatre seen in soft muted colours: a surgeon extends an open hand and a nurse places an instrument in it, both focused and calm.
meaning-use-concept: An open wooden toolbox in which the tools (hammer, screwdriver, ruler, glue pot) each have a small word-shaped tag, laid out neatly on a workbench.
meaning-use-example: Three small scenes in a row of the same person saying a word: smiling at a café, turning away from a nosy colleague, and staring at rain from a window with crossed arms.
family-concept: A family portrait of four generations: each person shares some features with a neighbour (the same nose, the same eyes, the same hair) but no single feature runs through them all.
family-example: A park scene with people playing chess on a bench, kids playing catch, someone playing solitaire, and a child playing pretend with a cardboard crown.
life-concept: A bustling village square: people greeting, a market stall weighing apples, children playing, a small funeral procession at the edge; speech is suggested only by gestures.
life-example: A traveller at a restaurant table holding coins over the bill, hesitating, while a waiter waits politely.
going-on-concept: A teacher and a pupil at a blackboard showing a repeated geometric pattern of dots and paired strokes; the visual pattern runs smoothly then forks into two possible continuations at the edge of the board.
going-on-example: Hands knitting a scarf, the pattern of stitches visibly repeating, a printed pattern card lying beside the yarn.
interpretation-concept: A traveller standing at a wooden signpost in open country; the signpost points down a path, and the traveller is already walking that path.
interpretation-example: A cook tasting soup from a wooden spoon over a pot, a recipe card on the counter with a long trail of tiny footnotes spilling off its edge.
private-concept: A small open diary on a nightstand, with the same small non-alphabetic ink mark repeated in several cells of an unlabelled diary grid, lit by a bedside lamp at night.
private-example: A person sitting on the edge of a bed in the morning, pen in hand over a diary, pausing with a thoughtful, unsure expression.
beetle-concept: A row of people each holding a small closed wooden box close to their chest, each peeking into their own box; one of them is speaking to the others.
beetle-example: Two friends at a market stall smelling fresh coriander, one wrinkling their nose, the other smiling.
criteria-concept: A city street in two panels: one with rain visibly falling on umbrellas, the other dry sky but wet pavement and a street-cleaning truck around the corner.
criteria-example: A person pulling a toothpick out of a cake in an oven, examining it in warm kitchen light.
aspects-concept: A large wire-frame cube drawn on paper on an easel, with two faint viewers on either side seeing it from above and from below.
aspects-example: A person on a train looking up from a book, struck by a passenger across the aisle, with a small inset memory-frame showing a sibling with the same smile.
hinges-concept: A heavy wooden door swinging open on two large iron hinges, the hinges lit warmly and the door slightly blurred as it moves.
hinges-example: A person at a kitchen table holding a paper bank statement, circling one line with a pencil, a calculator nearby.
doubt-concept: A person walking back up a garden path to try a front-door handle, while a second, faint version of the same person stands confused in an empty, featureless space.
doubt-example: A person on a bus checking their keys and looking back over their shoulder toward home.
colour-concept: A painter’s table with paint tubes, a sheet of white paper beside snow outside a window, and a pane of tinted glass casting coloured light.
colour-example: Hands holding up a pane of green glass and a pane of milky glass in front of a window, the view through one green, through the other cloudy.
will-concept: A calm figure walking along a path of evenly spaced footprints, contrasted with a faint second figure being shoved by a large hand, the two separated by a clear line.
will-example: A person ordering coffee at a café counter at 8 a.m. while a friend nearby smiles knowingly, holding up a clock.
grammar-concept: A chessboard seen from above with a carved king, soft arrows showing its possible one-square moves, and the other pieces at rest.
grammar-example: Two people playing chess on a porch where one king has been replaced by a bottle cap, both players perfectly serious.
ritual-concept: A person by a window gently kissing a framed photograph, a candle and flowers on the sill, evening light.
ritual-example: A family around a birthday cake as a child blows out the candles, everyone clapping.
psychology-concept: Three overlapping circles drawn on paper on a desk, with a small figure in each: one holding their hand after touching a stove, one wincing, one with a calm inner glow.
psychology-example: A parent kneeling to comfort a toddler with a bumped knee on a playground, the toddler mid-cry.
method-concept: A glass bottle on a windowsill with a fly inside; the bottle’s neck is open to the sky and a soft beam of light shows the way out.
method-example: A hand switching on a lamp in a familiar living room, the furniture becoming clear, a person who had bumped a chair now smiling.
reading-lab-concept: A reading desk with an open book, a pencil, small plain sticky tabs marking different sections and a magnifying glass resting on one paragraph.
reading-lab-example: A close-up of a page rendered as abstract, non-legible lines of ink: one line is underlined, and a pencil bracket carefully draws attention to a small qualifying introductory phrase; a hand pauses with a pencil nearby.
daily-life-concept: A person walking through an ordinary day (breakfast, a bus, an office, a park) with a small notebook, pausing to jot down a word at each stop.
daily-life-example: A team around a whiteboard where a blank central circle splits into three branches ending in simple pictorial task icons, people nodding.
